headline: Your team can do more with AI than they think. Give me a quarter.
text_under_headline: I’m Manu. I’ve taught more than 5,000 people in 30 countries to work with AI. I meet your team where they are, build alongside them, and leave them able to keep going without me.

headline: You’ve already tried. You have the graveyard to prove it.
text_under_headline: Most companies that started with AI have a quiet pile of pilots that never earned their keep. The demo worked. The rollout didn’t. That isn’t anyone’s fault. The tools moved faster than anyone had time to learn them.

headline: Teach, build, hand over. Your people are in every step.
text_under_headline: For a mid-sized company, twelve weeks is enough to change how a team works with AI. Not because I do it for you, but because by the end your team is doing it themselves.

headline: Things I’ve learned teaching 5,000 people.
What people say after the class.
What a quarter needs from you.
text_under_headline: I can move fast. I can’t move a company that isn’t ready to move. Better you hear that now than in week six.

headline: Thirty minutes. Tell me what you’ve tried. I’ll tell you what I’d change.
text_under_headline: No slides, no prep, no pitch deck.

headline: You’re paying for AI. The work still happens the old way.
text_under_headline: I’m Manu. I take one piece of work your team repeats, set it up in the AI tools you already have, and stay until your team uses it without me. That’s the whole service.

headline: I fix one thing at a time. That’s the honest version of “AI at scale.”
text_under_headline: Most AI efforts stall because they try to change everything at once. I pick one piece of work, get it running, and hand it over. Then we decide whether there’s a second one.

headline: For the person who approves the AI bill and can’t point to what changed.
text_under_headline: You’re not behind. You bought the tools and people use them. The work just looks the same as it did last year.

headline: Right now, your best AI work lives in one person’s chat history.
text_under_headline: That’s a habit, not a change in how the company works. When that person is on holiday, it stops.

headline: What I can’t do for you.
text_under_headline: If you need the whole company reinvented by next quarter, I’m the wrong person. Better you hear that here than three months in.

headline: Thirty minutes. Bring one piece of work. I’ll tell you if it’s worth doing.
text_under_headline: No slides. No prep document. Nothing to buy.

headline: AI transformation at scale means one job other people can run.
text_under_headline: Not a private chat. Not a crowd of consultants arriving to redo the company.

headline: The unit of work is one job the company already does.
text_under_headline: Scale means the change can be repeated inside the company. It does not mean a thousand people next quarter.

headline: This is for the person who has to say whether the week changed.
text_under_headline: The tools are on the bill. One enthusiast is not the company. You can still say yes.

headline: It spreads when the next person can do the job without the first person’s chat.
text_under_headline: A private habit is not a company change. The setup has to live where other people can use it.

headline: One job made usable is not a transformation of the company.
text_under_headline: If “at scale” means a board-level remake next quarter, this is the wrong door.

headline: We name one job. If it is not worth doing, I say so and we stop.
text_under_headline: Half an hour. No strategy document. No second purchase.
